title.narrative: Samoa Agriculture & Fisheries Productivity and Marketing Project

description.narrative: The development objective of Agriculture and Fisheries Productivity and Marketing Project for Samoa is to increase the productivity and access to markets by selected producers, to improve management of targeted productive natural resources and, in the event of an eligible crisis or emergency, to provide an immediate response to the eligible crisis or emergency. This project has four components. 1) The first component, Strengthening National Institutions, aims at creating an enabling environment for increased productivity and access to markets for target farming and fishing households and private sector along the targeted value-chains. It has the following subcomponents: (i) Institutional capacity building for crops and livestock; and (ii) Strengthening management of the region's shared oceanic and coastal fisheries. 2) The second component, Strengthening the performance of selected value-chains, has the following two subcomponents: (i) Public Good Infrastructure; and (ii) Matching Grant Program. 3) The third component, ASCD establishment and project management, Monitoring and Evaluation, and communications, aims to support the establishment of the agriculture sector coordination division (ASCD). 4) The fourth component, Contingency Emergency Response, aims to draw from the uncommitted grant resources under the project from other project components to cover emergency response.

To increase the productivity and access to markets by selected producers, to improve management of targeted productive natural resources and, in the event of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, to provide an immediate response to the Eligible Crisis or Emergency.

title.narrative: Average value of sales of fruit and vegetables growers and livestock producers (in SAT)

comment.narrative: Target not met. A 20% increase in value of sales was expected for fruits and vegetable farmers and 10 % for livestock farmers. The final amount (US$3,404 annual average) reflects an independent ICR analysis of reported sales for (1) 58 fruits and vegetable beneficiaries of MGP-1 (reported at Year 3), and of 2 MGP-2 enterprises, reported after project completion; and (2) 351 cattle, 42 piggery, 16 sheep, and 16 poultry beneficiaries for MGP-1 (reported at Year 3), and of 2 cattle and 1 piggery MGP-2 enterprises, reported at project completion. The results indicate those sales represented a 30% decline from baseline values ( 38% for vegetables and fruits and 15% for livestock) with likely explanations being herd accumulation and high proportion of fa’alavelave (for livestock), mortality among poultry farmers, fallow plots (for vegetables), home consumption, and imaturity of fruit trees planted at the time Year 3 survey was conducted (late 2024).

title.narrative: Land area under sustainable farm management practices

comment.narrative: The indicator measures, In hectares, the land area for which new and/or improved sustainable farm management practices have been introduced. Land is the terrestial biologically productive system comprising soil, vegetation, and the associated ecological and hydrological processes; Adoption refers to change of practice or change in the use of a technology promoted or introduced by the project; Sustainable Farm Management (SFM) practices refers to a combination of at least two technologies and approaches to increase land quality and restore degraded lands for example, agronomic, vegetative, structural, and management measures that, applied as a combination, increase the connectivity between protected areas, forest land, rangeland and agriculture land.

title.narrative: Land area under sustainable farm management practices

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. The PAD defined the indicator as measuring, in hectares, the land area for which new and/or improved sustainable farm management practices have been introduced. The result is as reported by MAF and reflects increase in land area by beneficiaries adopting new technologies and expanded operation to new areas. comment.narrative: Target exceeded. This citizen engagement indicator reflects the proportion of three MGP beneficiaries rating their sub-projects as “Excellent/Very Satisfied” or “Satisfactory/Good/Moderately Satisfactory,” based on an independent ICR team analysis of the latest MAF and CSSP beneficiary surveys. The MAF survey focused on MGP-1 and MGP-2 beneficiaries, whereas CSSP surveyed MGP-3, MGP-2 and 27 MGP-1 beneficiaries. The two surveys gave fairly consistent answers: using MAF'survey for MGP-2 beneficiaries, 76.5% of 831 beneficiaries rated their satisfaction with their sub-projects as Very Satisfied and 12.6% as Moderately Satisfied (total 89.9%).

title.narrative: Industry and Competent Authority are operating with newly established standard procedures for seafood export

comment.narrative: Target mostly met. The indicator, measuring access to export markets, corresponds to interim targets of the three sub-indicators achieved in the period. It is considered mostly met, as the Competent Authority carried out the necessary audits, issued health certificates and provided training to the two major seafood export companies in Samoa while they were operational. However, one (Apia Deep Sea Fishing) ceased operations in Samoa in 2024 and the second (Apia Export Fish Packers) sold only locally in 2025. Hence, the results represent the totality of active seafood export enterprises in Samoa at project closing.
